skills.trigger: When evaluating interval changes in a mediastinal mass on serial chest X-rays to distinguish between residual disease, recurrence, or resolution.
steps: Compare the width and density of the mediastinal silhouette on the initial and follow-up frontal views to assess for size reduction or enlargement.
Trace the tracheal air column on both studies to determine if deviation persists, resolves, or worsens relative to the mass size change.
Interpret persistent tracheal deviation despite mass size reduction as evidence of residual mass effect rather than complete resolution or hematoma (which typically lacks significant mass effect).
Differentiate residual mass from recurrence by noting that recurrence usually presents with increased size or new/worsening displacement compared to the baseline.
